messages:
Vanessa Ortiz: hey folks — quick clarification needed for burst pools isolation. are we putting burst pools in the same physical cluster as hosted, or separate? need to lock this down before we finalize labels/topology.

Nina Petrova: depends what you mean by “same cluster” — same k8s control plane vs same underlying GPU cell. current draft assumes separate node pools but same k8s cluster in each region.

Keiko Yamamoto: if same k8s cluster, we need really tight taints/affinity so hosted schedulers never land on burst nodes and vice versa. also want to ensure we’re not sharing the same HPA signals.

Vikram Singh: from data plane perspective: we can keep them in same cluster if routing is strict (burst pools are a different fleet label + separate service discovery). but we need to guarantee no cross-tenant leakage in logs/metrics and no accidental “fallback to hosted” when burst saturates.

Mina Haddad: routing will treat burst as an explicit target pool (baseline dedicated -> burst pool -> deny/fallback model) but we need the infra contract: is burst capacity carved out of hosted headroom or physically isolated?

Vanessa Ortiz: the intent is “controlled shared burst pools” but *not* impacting hosted commitments. if it’s the same cluster as hosted, folks will (reasonably) ask if contention can hurt hosted p99.

Sean Gallagher: +1, for SRE the question is: can burst saturation page us because hosted p99 drifts? if yes, we need a very clear circuit breaker and hard capacity partitioning.

Samantha Roy: on telemetry side, if it’s same cluster/cell, our capacity signals need to distinguish hosted-reserved vs burst-reserved. otherwise admission control will think there’s headroom when there isn’t.

Nina Petrova: proposal we discussed last week: burst pools share the *regional control plane* but run in dedicated “burst cells” (separate GPU nodegroups + separate kube namespace + network policy). hosted and burst do not share the same nodegroups. we can still be in same k8s cluster, but with:
- node taints: `redwood.ai/pool=burst:NoSchedule`
- required node affinity in burst serving deployment
- separate cluster autoscaler profiles
- quota guard: burst nodes excluded from hosted reservations

Keiko Yamamoto: can we also enforce via admission controller? (prevent any non-burst workload from scheduling onto burst nodes even if taints get messed up). belts + suspenders.

Vanessa Ortiz: yep, we can add a validating policy in the cluster (OPA/Gatekeeper) or at least a CI check in infra repo. would like a “can’t accidentally allocate reserved dedicated onto burst nodes” guarantee.

Peter Holtz: also important: are burst pools in same VPC subnets as hosted? if yes, customer security reviews will ask about blast radius + traffic inspection. if no, then we need to document cross-subnet routing for control plane.

Nina Petrova: networking draft: same VPC, separate subnets + security groups. no L4 access between hosted serving pods and burst serving pods except via shared control plane endpoints. customer traffic still goes to dedicated ingress; routing decides whether backend is baseline or burst. no direct burst->hosted hop.

Mina Haddad: ok but then discovery endpoints need to be explicit. we should not allow “hosted endpoints” in the same service registry query for dedicated tenants. can we get a hard separation in fleet discovery? i.e. `pool_class=hosted|dedicated|burst`.

Vanessa Ortiz: yes — that’s the label taxonomy we’re drafting (`pool_class`, `tenant_scope`, `gpu_type`, `region`). burst pools will be `tenant_scope=shared` but `pool_class=burst`. baseline dedicated is `tenant_scope=tenant` + `pool_class=dedicated`.

Sean Gallagher: what’s the failure mode if someone mislabels a nodegroup and it shows up as `pool_class=dedicated`? do we have a detection alert?

Samantha Roy: we can emit a periodic “pool inventory” metric with expected counts by `pool_class` and alert on drift (e.g. burst nodes showing up under dedicated label). also can compare against infra source-of-truth.

Keiko Yamamoto: for guardrails, I’d like this spelled out in the topology doc: burst pools are allowed to be shared *across dedicated tenants* but must never be shared with hosted. shared hardware cell w/ hosted = no-go for v1.

Nina Petrova: agree. to be explicit: v1: burst pools do not share GPU nodes with hosted and are not used for hosted traffic. whether they share the same k8s cluster is an implementation detail, but we’ll document the isolation controls.

Mina Haddad: :thumbsup: can we add a one-pager section for routing: “burst is not a hosted fallback” and list allowed transitions. keeps everyone aligned.

Vanessa Ortiz: action items:
1) Nina to update Confluence burst pool topology doc with explicit statements re: hosted separation + network/subnet notes.
2) Keiko to propose admission-controller/Gatekeeper rule + taints/affinity enforcement checklist.
3) Samantha to add telemetry requirement: pool inventory + label drift alert.
4) Mina/Vikram to add a small routing contract blurb (allowed pool transitions) that infra can reference.

Vikram Singh: +1, I’ll draft the routing contract text and share in #architecture for review.

Sean Gallagher: please also include “operational kill switch” location in the doc (who can disable burst per region) — we’ll get asked in incident reviews.

Vanessa Ortiz: good call — I’ll add that to the doc update as well. thanks all.
